question.text: Which of these southern US cities will have Tesla Robotaxi service on December 31, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the availability status of Tesla Robotaxi service for Atlanta, GA and Jacksonville, FL as of December 31, 2026 (i.e., using the most recent information before January 1, 2027) according to [Tesla's Robotaxi](https://www.tesla.com/robotaxi) information portal. A city listed as "Coming soon" does not count.
question.fine_print: If the main resolution source does not provide the information on the target date, other credible sources such as the [Robotaxi support page](https://www.tesla.com/support/robotaxi#availability) or credible sources may be used.

research:
I've finished searching and am writing up the findings now.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16: I couldn't read tesla.com/robotaxi or tesla.com/support/robotaxi. Both return "Access Denied" (HTTP 403) to automated requests, so I have no direct reading of the portal. [tesla.com/robotaxi](https://www.tesla.com/robotaxi)
- 2026-11-09 (latest snapshot from a third party): Tesla's map shows 9 live areas: Austin, SF Bay Area (with a safety driver), Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Fort Worth and San Antonio. **Jacksonville is "Coming soon."** Las Vegas and Phoenix are also "Coming soon." **Atlanta is not listed at all.** [ChargePort tracker](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Neither city has live service. Jacksonville is "Coming soon," which does not count. Atlanta has no Tesla listing of any kind.
- 2026-10-29: DockDuty says there are no Tesla Robotaxi or Cybercab rides in Atlanta and Atlanta is not on the Coming Soon list. Waymo (through Uber) is the active operator there. [DockDuty Atlanta](https://dockduty.com/atlanta.html)
- I couldn't open the Reddit "Cybercab spotting in Atlanta" post, and no news outlet has reported an Atlanta Cybercab sighting. A Cybercab seen on the road is not a service listing. There are also reports of Tesla moving Cybercabs around the country for unclear reasons. [pulse.bot](https://www.pulse.bot/transportation/news/tesla-has-sent-cybercabs-around-the-country-not-clear-why-6c7d1fea-7c60-4898-a366-0d766db1c4bb/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-14: Tesla opened invitation-only personal Cybercab sales at $29,990, plus a $299/month autonomy subscription, with deliveries in December. Coverage did not mention new cities. [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/business/tech/tesla-opens-cybercab-sales-to-select-customers-for-29990)
- 2026-11-09: Robotaxi launched in San Antonio, the 8th city by Tesla's count (the 9 areas above include Fort Worth separately). [Teslarati](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-robotaxi-enters-newest-city-san-antonio/); [Tesla Oracle](https://www.teslaoracle.com/2026/11/09/after-fort-worth-tesla-launches-robotaxi-service-in-san-antonio-texas-today-nov-9-now-available-in-8-cities/)
- 2026-11-02: Fort Worth launched with a single downtown zone. [Tesla North](https://teslanorth.com/2026/11/01/tesla-robotaxi-fort-worth-launch/)
- 2026-10-26: News4Jax said Tesla has given no launch date or service area for Jacksonville. Background: Florida law allows driverless vehicles and blocks local rules, and the city's JTA NAVI autonomous shuttle pauses on 2027-01-01. [News4Jax](https://www.news4jax.com/news/local/2026/10/26/tesla-robotaxis-are-listed-as-coming-soon-to-jacksonville-when-could-rides-start/); [Action News Jax](https://www.actionnewsjax.com/news/local/tesla-lists-jacksonville-robotaxi-service-coming-soon-no-launch-date-announced/E22ICBNSCZFT3FWAEL3MN555EQ/)
- 2026-10-21: Tesla's Robotaxi account listed Jacksonville, Las Vegas, Phoenix and San Antonio as "coming soon." That was the first time Tesla named Jacksonville. [Tesla Oracle](https://www.teslaoracle.com/2026/10/23/tesla-announces-robotaxi-launch-in-four-more-cities-releases-safety-data-via-new-website-no-kittens-were-hurt/)
- 2026-10-21: On the Q3 earnings call, the CFO said Cybercab would reach "some other cities before the end of this year," with Dallas Cybercab rides first in November. Tesla is aiming for 24/7 service by the end of 2026. [Tesla North](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/21/tesla-q3-2026-call-takeaways/); [Not a Tesla App](https://notateslaapp.com/news/4867/tesla-q3-2026-earnings-call-recap-everything-you-need-to-know)

## 4. Base rates
- Time from "coming soon" to launch varies a lot. San Antonio was listed on 10-21 and launched on 11-09, 19 days later. Phoenix was described as "Preparations Underway" in Tesla's Q2 disclosure, is still not live, and has stayed on the list since 10-21. Las Vegas has a Nevada permit but no riders yet. [ChargePort](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker)
- 2026 launch dates so far: Dallas and Houston (04-18), Miami (07-03), Orlando and Tampa (07-21), Fort Worth (11-02), San Antonio (11-09). That is roughly one launch batch every 1 to 3 months, and the pace has picked up in November. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- Florida launches have all started as unsupervised service. Tesla already runs three Florida metros, so it has operating experience in the state. Every city that has gone live in 2026 had been announced or listed by Tesla first. I found no case of a city going from not listed at all to live within about 6 weeks, though Fort Worth's listing history is unclear.
- 2026-04-01: CleanTechnica listed Atlanta among Tesla pilot cities, but later sources contradict this and it looks unreliable. [CleanTechnica](https://cleantechnica.com/2026/04/01/tesla-robotaxis-will-be-covering-70-of-us-population-in-2-weeks/)

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Which states will robotaxi be offered to this year?" (before 2027-01-01), prices as of 2026-11-16: Georgia 0.13, Florida 0.90, Nevada 0.53, Arizona 0.89. Caveat: I didn't verify that this market tracks Tesla specifically. Florida is probably already satisfied by Miami, Orlando and Tampa, so that price tells you nothing about Jacksonville. Georgia at 0.13 is a rough proxy for Atlanta.
- Manifold: 94% that Tesla gives paid public Cybercab rides outside Texas by 2027-04-30. 63% for driverless service in 10 or more metros beyond Austin by 2027-08-01. Neither is specific to these two cities.
- I found no market specifically on Jacksonville.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Possible Jacksonville launch at any point. The two most recent cities launched about a week apart, and San Antonio took 19 days from listing to launch.
- Any Atlanta "coming soon" listing on the portal or the @robotaxi X account. Without one, Atlanta going live by 12-31 would break the listing-before-launch pattern seen in 2026.
- Cybercab rides starting in Dallas and "other cities" before year-end (CFO guidance), and personal Cybercab deliveries in December.
- Phoenix and Las Vegas launches, which would show how quickly Tesla is working through its "coming soon" list.
- Tesla's Q4 delivery report in early January comes after resolution.

- **Atlanta:** I found no case of Tesla going from no listing at all to live in under about six weeks, apart from the possible Fort Worth exception above. There are about 6.5 weeks left. I found no Georgia regulatory news about Tesla.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Possible launches of the three remaining "Coming soon" cities (Phoenix, Las Vegas, Jacksonville) as Tesla pushes for year-end. Tesla has often timed launches to make year-end deadlines.
- Cybercab deliveries in December, and any Dallas Cybercab launch, could take operational focus.
- Federal safety regulators are reviewing a petition alleging that about 1,000 Tesla robotaxis speed through school zones. A recall or probe could slow expansion.
- Tesla's Q4 deliveries report in early January comes after resolution. Any city announcements Tesla makes on X before December 31 would matter.
- Watch whether Atlanta gets added as "Coming soon", which would be the first official signal there.

(b) Status quo: neither city is live. Jacksonville is listed as "Coming soon," which does not count. Atlanta is not listed at all. If nothing changed, the answer would be "In neither city."

(c) Base rates:
- **Time from "coming soon" to launch:** this has ranged from 19 days (San Antonio) to more than 4 months and still waiting (Phoenix). Phoenix and Las Vegas, both listed on Oct 21, are still not live after nearly 4 weeks.

- **Rough starting estimates:** about 45-55% that a "coming soon" city launches within roughly 10 weeks of listing, and well under 10% for an unlisted city to go live within 6 weeks.

(d) Strongest evidence:
- **Tesla's listing and statements:**
  - On 2026-10-21, Tesla first listed Jacksonville as coming soon.
  - On the same day, the CFO said Tesla is pushing to expand before year-end.
- **Launch pace:**
  - Fort Worth launched on 11-02 and San Antonio on 11-09, so the pace is speeding up.
  - Tesla has existing Florida operations in Miami, Orlando and Tampa, all unsupervised.
  - Tesla historically rushes to meet year-end targets.
- **Atlanta:**
  - It was not on the list as of 11-09, and DockDuty confirmed on 10-29 that there is no Tesla presence there.
  - Kalshi has Georgia at 0.13. That market is probably Tesla-specific, since Waymo already operates in Atlanta.
  - There was a Reddit sighting of a Cybercab in Atlanta, but Tesla is also moving Cybercabs around the country for testing.
- **No firm date:** there is no Jacksonville launch date, and News4Jax (10-26) reported no service area yet.

(e) Unexpected scenario: Tesla does a year-end push, announcing Atlanta and launching it within days, possibly with Cybercabs, while Jacksonville slips because of geofence or validation delays. That would give "Atlanta not Jacksonville." Alternatively, both launch in a December batch.

- **Jacksonville:** I started from about 50% and moved up slightly to about 52%. Florida experience and the November momentum push it up. The pending Phoenix and Las Vegas listings and Tesla's history of slipping timelines hold it down.
- **Atlanta:** about 10%, anchored near Kalshi's 0.13 for Georgia and nudged down because Atlanta is not even listed.
- **Correlation:** the two are positively correlated, because a year-end push would lift both.
